cards.claim: Jonathan Cantwell represents or is associated with Club Deportivo Ñublense.
cards.quote: Jonathan's eyes landed on a vintage Club Deportivo Ñublense jersey, its red and blue stripes a stark contrast to the drab, European teams he was accustomed to. A gruff, yet kind-eyed man, introduced himself as Don Pedro, the café owner and a die-hard Ñublense fan. As they chatted, Jonathan learned that the club was struggling to find its footing in the Chilean league, and Don Pedro lamented the lack of talent and resources. Jonathan's competitive spirit stirred, and he found himself offering words of encouragement, sharing stories of his own struggles on the cycling circuit. Don Pedro's eyes lit up, and he exclaimed, "You know, amigo, we could use a man of your mettle on our team. Not on the pitch, of course, but as a fitness coach, perhaps?" Jonathan laughed, but the seed was planted. As he finished his meal and prepared to leave, Don Pedro pressed a Ñublense scarf into his hands, saying, "You never know, Jonathan.

cards.claim: Jonathan Cantwell represents or represented V Australia.
cards.quote: But it was his association with the continental team, V Australia, that cemented his place in the annals of cycling history. The year was 2009, and Cantwell was on the cusp of a breakthrough. Having already made a name for himself in the Australian domestic circuit, he was hungry for a bigger challenge. That's when V Australia, a relatively new team on the block, came knocking. Founded in 2009, V Australia was on a mission to become a force to be reckoned with in the world of professional cycling. They were looking for riders who shared their vision, their passion, and their commitment to excellence. Cantwell fit the bill perfectly. On August 12, 2009, Cycling News reported that Cantwell had signed with V Australia, joining a talented roster of riders that included the likes of Chris Sutton, Bernard Sulzberger, and David Kemp.
